about.title: Marysville Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Marysville households rely daily on tools, appliances, vehicles, and consumer goods that are supposed to work safely as designed. When one fails — a faulty wiring harness, a defective ladder rung, a mislabeled chemical, a malfunctioning car part — the resulting injury can upend a family's routine fast. Yuba County residents dealing with these injuries often aren't sure who's responsible: the manufacturer, the distributor, or the store that sold it. California law gives injured consumers a real path forward, and getting the timing right matters, since the product itself is often the most important piece of evidence in the case. We review product liability claims for Marysville residents at no cost — we'll examine the product, the injury, and the circumstances to help determine what legal options may exist. That first conversation costs nothing and carries no obligation.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California generally allows injured consumers to hold a maker liable for a defective product without proving negligence — only that the defect caused the harm. We can help identify which type of defect applies to your situation.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable under California product liability law. This matters in a smaller market like Marysville, where a product may have passed through several hands before reaching you.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Claim
items.desc: Because the defective item itself is often the central piece of evidence, keeping it safe and unaltered after an injury is critical. We can advise on proper handling before it's lost, discarded, or repaired.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not usually. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, rather than proving the manufacturer acted negligently. We can review your situation and explain which theory best fits your facts.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, if you can do so safely. Don't repair it, throw it away, or return it to the store, since it may serve as key evidence in a future claim.
